title: Inverse systems satisfying finite-cover lifting define site points
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with finite limits. Let $(I,\geq,U_i,f_{ii'})$ be a directed inverse system of objects of $\mathcal C$: $I$ is a nonempty directed poset, each $i\geq i'$ has $f_{ii'}:U_i\to U_{i'}$, and $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{i'i''}f_{ii'}=f_{ii''}$. Define $u(W)=\varinjlim_{i\in I}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(U_i,W)$. Assume that for every covering family $\{W_k\to W\}_{k\in K}$ and every $f\in u(W)$ there are $k\in K$ and $g\in u(W_k)$ whose image in $u(W)$ is $f$. Then $u$ commutes with finite limits and sends every covering family to a jointly surjective family. Consequently $u$ is a point of the site in the sense of Tag 00YC (Proposition proposition-point-limits), and the point-to-topos construction of Tag 00YA (Lemma lemma-point-site-topos) gives a geometric morphism $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism] whose inverse image satisfies the canonical identification $p^{-1}\mathcal F\cong\varinjlim_{i\in I}\mathcal F(U_i)$ for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$.

proof.text: Use the stated size convention and the chosen colimit of representables. Evaluation preserves this colimit. Types.jointly_surjective_of_isColimit gives representatives [i,a], and Types.FilteredColimit.isColimit_eq_iff' gives eventual equality for representatives at the same index. The canonical coprojections commute with postcomposition and with transition maps; these are homMk_map and homMk_transition in the Lean proof.

proof.text: Each representable Hom(U_i,-) preserves finite limits. The filtered-colimit/finite-limit interchange [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] makes the property of preserving finite limits closed under I-shaped colimits. Apply ObjectProperty.preservesFiniteLimits.prop_colimit to the representable diagram. This proves PreservesFiniteLimits u.

source.place: Tag 002W (lemma-directed-commutes); applied to the representable finite-limit comparison used in Sites Tag 00YC

proof.text: The functor S is the composite of inclusion of sheaves into presheaves, restriction along the opposite inverse-system diagram, and the I-colimit functor. Inclusion and restriction preserve finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise]. The final factor preserves finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits]. Thus S preserves finite limits also for sets in the larger stated universe.

The given hcover is exactly joint surjectivity for every covering family. Every covering presieve has a presentation Presieve.ofArrows with a small indexing type (Presieve.exists_eq_ofArrows), so this gives lifting for every covering presieve. Empty coverings are included: a lift cannot exist, so the target fibre is empty.

source.place: Tag 00YC (proposition-point-limits), conditions (1) and (2), and Tag 00Y5 (definition-point), conditions (1) and (2)

proof.text: Define e:I^op -> Elements(u) by i |-> (U_i,[i,id]) and the transition morphisms. It is initial: a representative x=[i,a] gives a pointed arrow e(i)->(W,x); if two pointed arrows from e(i) have the same target, their representing maps have equal colimit classes, so a later transition equalizes them. This is Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered, applied using homMk_surjective and homMk_eq. Consequently the opposite of e, precomposed with the double-opposite equivalence, is final. Its composite with the neighbourhood projection is definitionally inverseSystemOppositeDiagram U. Functor.Final.colimIso, whiskered with restriction and then the sheaf inclusion, gives a canonical natural isomorphism T ≅ S, not just separate bijections on objects. The initial functor also gives initial smallness of Elements(u).

source.place: The neighbourhood category and equation-stalk immediately before Tag 00Y5 (definition-point); explicit comparison for the inverse system in the proof of Tag 00YQ (proposition-criterion-points)

proof.text: Finite-limit preservation gives cofilteredness of Elements(u) by Functor.isCofiltered_elements. Extend the covering-presieve lifting property to the generated topology by induction on Precoverage.Saturate. Generated coverings inherit the chosen lift; the maximal sieve lifts by the identity. For a pullback, first lift the image of the chosen element, then take a cone over the two resulting pointed objects and equalize their parallel maps to the original pointed object. Their underlying composites coincide, so the resulting arrow lies in the pullback sieve and lifts the element. For transitivity lift first along the first sieve, then along the covering pullback of the second sieve, and compose. These are all cases of saturation. Together with cofilteredness and initial smallness this constructs a Mathlib GrothendieckTopology.Point with fibre u.

For the constructed site point, use Mathlib Point.skyscraperSheafFunctor and Point.skyscraperSheafAdjunction. Their direct image is R(E)(W)=Map(u(W),E), with the gluing and currying proof of Stacks Tags 00Y7 and 00Y8 already proved in Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.Point.Skyscraper. This gives T ⊣ R for the neighbourhood stalk T.

source.place: Tag 00Y8 (lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf), proof of (1), with its sheaf gluing written out

proof.text: Transport the skyscraper adjunction across the canonical natural isomorphism T ≅ S from Step 5 using Adjunction.ofNatIsoLeft. With finite-limit preservation of S from Step 3, this defines the geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism] with inverse image exactly S. The required natural isomorphism of its inverse image with inverseSystemSectionColimitFunctor is therefore the identity.

lean.statement: theorem inverseSystemSitePoint {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] [HasFiniteLimits C] (J : Precoverage C) (hJ : J.IsSiteForCoverings) {I : Type u} [PartialOrder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (U : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ C) (hcover : ∀ {K : Type u} {W : C} (V : K → C) (a : ∀ k, V k ⟶ W), Presieve.ofArrows V a ∈ J W → ∀ f : (inverseSystemHomFunctor U).obj W, ∃ (k : K) (g : (inverseSystemHomFunctor U).obj (V k)), (inverseSystemHomFunctor U).map (a k) g = f) : PreservesFiniteLimits (inverseSystemHomFunctor U) ∧ (∀ (K : Type u) (W : C) (V : K → C) (a : ∀ k, V k ⟶ W) (_ : Presieve.ofArrows V a ∈ J W) (f : (inverseSystemHomFunctor U).obj W), ∃ (k : K) (g : (inverseSystemHomFunctor U).obj (V k)), (inverseSystemHomFunctor U).map (a k) g = f) ∧ ∃ (p : GeometricMorphism (Type (max u w)) (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type (max u w)))), Nonempty (p.inverse ≅ inverseSystemSectionColimitFunctor.{w} J.toGrothendieck U)
lean.note: Maintainer fix 2026-10-18: the site is the recorded rendering of def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology (Precoverage J with J.IsSiteForCoverings, sheaves for J.toGrothendieck); sheaf values are Type (max u w), as in the citer finitarySite_enoughPoints; the inverse-image clause is a natural isomorphism p.inverse ≅ inverseSystemSectionColimitFunctor (F ↦ colim_i F(U_i) with its canonical action on morphisms), replacing a per-sheaf Nonempty isomorphism of sets, which only asserted equal cardinality.
